amanda: Hey team — seeing a sudden spike of 504s and duplicate billable requests after we bumped our service to go-sdk v0.13.0. Most client logs show ctx canceled + later a retry that succeeds. Any known issues with HTTP2 / transport cancel behavior?

ben: Do you have a tiny repro or the http.Client/Transport config you use? Also which Go version?

amanda: Go 1.20, sample code below (trimmed):

```go
tr := &http.Transport{
    MaxIdleConns:        100,
    MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
    IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
    TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{
    Transport: tr,
    Timeout:   0, // we use context for timeouts
}
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", apiURL, bytes.NewReader(body))
resp, err := client.Do(req)
if err != nil {
    // sometimes get "context canceled" here, then SDK retries and a second request succeeds
}
// we do read body etc.
```

mila: Two quick things: 1) if the SDK has automatic retries it may be issuing a new request after your ctx cancelled call returned — that can look like "duplicate" attempts. 2) HTTP/2 stream cancellation behavior is tricky: canceling the context doesn't necessarily tear down the connection, so the server may still receive the in-flight stream.

carlos: FWIW we've seen similar with Go's http2: CancelRequest is deprecated; Request.WithContext cancels at the request-level but streams may linger until server signals. If the SDK retry wrapper reuses the same http.Client/Transport, the retry can be sent on the same connection. If the original request actually reached the server, you get two billable operations.

ben: Can you share which retry policy the SDK is using (max attempts, backoff)? If it's blind retrying for non-idempotent POSTs you should either mark idempotency key or disable retry for that endpoint.

amanda: SDK defaults: 3 attempts exponential backoff. We didn't set idempotency. We thought context cancel would fully abort the attempt so later retry would be safe.

mila: Quick repro suggestion: set Transport.ForceAttemptHTTP2 = false (on Transport) to force HTTP/1.1 and see whether cancels behave differently. Also try adding ResponseHeaderTimeout and small IdleConnTimeout to make the client more eager to free connections.

carlos: Also ensure you always close resp.Body even on errors (some code paths forget). Example: `if resp != nil { io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body); resp.Body.Close() }` — leaving bodies open can keep streams around longer and confuse connection reuse.

ben: Another mitigation: configure the SDK to not retry on context.Canceled / deadline exceeded errors, or make the request idempotent (Idempotency-Key header). If you can't change the SDK, wrap the client's transport with a short-circuit that blocks retries after ctx.Done().

amanda: Thanks — we'll try: 1) add idempotency key 2) set ForceAttemptHTTP2=false and ResponseHeaderTimeout=3s 3) ensure resp.Body is always closed. Any guidance on permanent fix in SDK?

carlos: Long term, SDK should detect context cancellation and avoid scheduling retries that could lead to duplicate side-effects. Filing an issue with a minimal repro would help. Also we should add an option to treat POSTs as non-retriable by default unless an idempotency key is present. I'll open an internal ticket.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-1347 — investigate go-sdk retry semantics + http2 cancel interactions.

amanda: Great — confirming changes and repro steps, will report back with telemetry after a canary deploy. :thumbsup:
